title: Gaia radii show that 94% of 995 Gaia DR3 compact-companion ellipsoidal candidates are too large to fit in a Roche lobe; their radii match contact binaries, and survey velocities agree
abstract: Gaia DR3 lists 6,306 ellipsoidal variables (vari_compact_companion) as possible hosts of dark neutron-star or black-hole companions. Their minimum mass ratios assume one Roche-lobe-filling luminous star. We added the stellar radius. For one tidally distorted star with a companion of any mass, the luminosity radius must be between about 0.35 u and 0.51 u, with u = (G M1 P^2/4 pi^2)^(1/3). For the 995 candidates with parallax/error > 5, the median radius is 0.725 u. For 94% the median is above the Roche-lobe limit, and for 51% the full 95% interval is above it. 4,000 contact-like Gaia eclipsing binaries give 0.717 u, almost the same distribution. With a Teff-dependent radius-bias correction from 105,901 single dwarfs, 89% stay above the limit (64% with the largest correction). Only 49 candidates (1 of 16 testable high-q stars) have a median inside the window. Public RVs from LAMOST DR10, SDSS-V DR19 and DESI DR1 exist for 21 candidates. They prefer small orbital motion (sum ln B = -33 against K >= K_min; at most 30% of these stars at 95%). The 4 DESI exposures of one star limit K to 46 km/s against 114 km/s required. Two stars with large single LAMOST velocities need a second epoch. Limitations: only 16% of the catalogue has good parallaxes; GSP-Phot Teff and extinction have biases; most RV stars have one epoch. Most candidates are probably contact binaries, not dormant compact-object binaries.

display.caption: Luminosity radius in units of u = (G M1 P^2/4 pi^2)^(1/3) for 995 Gaia DR3 compact-companion candidates (blue) and 4,000 contact-like Gaia eclipsing binaries (orange). The green band shows the radii that one tidally distorted star with a dark companion of any mass can have. Dashed: candidates after a Teff-dependent radius-bias correction.
Luminosity radius (median and 95% interval) against Gaia period, with the window edges. Orange: the 16 testable stars of the main black-hole/neutron-star list (q_min 1 sigma > 1).

Left: survey velocities of 21 candidates minus the field-star median, in units of the minimum semi-amplitude K_min that a dark companion needs; grey bars show the field spread. Right: posterior for the fraction of stars with K in [K_min, 2 K_min].

citations.reason: Gomel et al. 2023: source of the vari_compact_companion candidates and of the amplitude formula; we test the single-luminous-star assumption.
Nagarajan et al. 2023 found low-mass companions for 14 bright candidates; our population test agrees.
O'Doherty et al. 2024: a contact binary that was classified as ellipsoidal; contamination warning.
El-Badry 2024 review states that most of the sample are contact binaries.
Andrae et al. 2018 bolometric correction for the G band.
Pecaut and Mamajek 2013 main-sequence mass and radius against Teff.
LAMOST DR10 v2.0 low-resolution catalogue via the public SQL service.
SDSS DR19 mwm_boss_allvisit per-visit radial velocities.
DESI DR1 Milky Way Survey radial velocities.
Campaign recipe for DESI DR1 per-exposure RVs and Data Lab access that we reused.
